articles.title: HHS Updates Peptide Compounding Rules for 503A Pharmacies
articles.summary: HHS has established new regulatory boundaries for peptide compounding by 503A pharmacies, a move directly impacting the availability and use of compounded GLP-1s and other specialty drugs. This development is significant for self-funded employers managing surging weight-loss drug costs and looking closely at compounded alternatives. The policy shift could alter plan utilization and safety strategies surrounding alternative drug sourcing.
articles.source_line: Source: The National Law Review; Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:43:15 GMT

articles.title: Industry Observers Analyze Department of Labor PBM Transparency and Disclosure Rule
articles.summary: Industry stakeholders are evaluating the potential operational and compliance impacts of the Department of Labor's new PBM Transparency and Disclosure Rule. The regulation increases scrutiny on self-funded employer health plans and their PBM partners regarding fee disclosures and fiduciary responsibilities under ERISA. This development directly impacts how self-funded employers audit and manage their pharmacy benefit contracts.
articles.source_line: Source: Drug Store News; Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:39:51 GMT

articles.title: Florida Fines PBMs $12.66 Million for Contract Violations
articles.summary: Florida Insurance Commissioner Mike Yaworsky penalized pharmacy benefit managers over $12.66 million for contract and regulatory violations. This enforcement action highlights increasing state-level scrutiny and oversight of PBM practices, directly impacting compliance and operational standards for benefit managers.
articles.source_line: Source: Alachua Chronicle; Mon, 09 Nov 2026 23:00:49 GMT

articles.title: CVS Health Restructuring Fails to Address Core PBM Market Pressures
articles.summary: Recent analysis suggests that corporate splitting or restructuring at CVS will not resolve the fundamental business pressures facing its PBM and retail pharmacy operations. For self-funded employers, ongoing instability and scrutiny of major legacy PBM models underscore the importance of exploring transparent, unbundled pharmacy benefit alternatives.

articles.title: Employers Increasingly Rely on Advisors Amid Benefits Cost Crisis
articles.summary: Escalating healthcare costs are driving self-funded and commercial employers to lean more heavily on benefits advisors and consultants for strategic cost management. This trend emphasizes the critical role advisors play in steering employers toward alternative PBM solutions and benefit plan designs to combat rising drug and medical spend.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:07:56 GMT

articles.title: CVS Leadership Questions Structural Breakup Strategy Amid Political Pressure
articles.summary: CVS executives express skepticism that spinning off retail pharmacy operations would appease lawmakers and regulators targeting PBM practices. This political scrutiny directly impacts the future operational structures and pricing transparency models of major PBMs, which is critical for self-funded employers monitoring market stability.
articles.source_line: Source: Crain's Chicago Business; Mon, 09 Nov 2026 23:59:02 GMT

articles.title: Ohio Attorney General Seeks to Streamline State Drug Pricing Litigation
articles.summary: The Ohio Attorney General has requested procedural changes to streamline an ongoing state drug pricing lawsuit involving pharmacy benefit management practices. This legal action highlights continued state-level regulatory scrutiny over PBM pricing models and contract transparency, which directly impacts employer plan sponsors operating in the region.

articles.title: Brown & Brown Survey Highlights How Healthcare Costs Reshape Employer Benefits Strategies
articles.summary: A new survey from Brown & Brown explores how rising healthcare costs are forcing self-funded employers to fundamentally rethink their benefits strategies. This highlights shifting employer demands for cost-management solutions, directly impacting how pharmacy benefits and plan designs are structured.

articles.title: Controlling Healthcare Costs Ranks as Top Strategic Priority for Employers by 2027
articles.summary: A new report highlights that plan sponsors view managing escalating healthcare costs as their primary strategic challenge moving into 2027. This focus directly impacts self-funded employers who are increasingly seeking aggressive cost containment strategies, particularly within pharmacy benefits. For PBMs and benefit advisors, this underscores the urgent demand for transparent pricing models and effective specialty drug management to retain employer clients.

articles.title: Plan Sponsors Shift Away from Deductibles and Out-of-Pocket Maximums
articles.summary: Self-funded employers are increasingly redesigning health plan benefits to eliminate deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums in an effort to remove financial barriers to care and improve utilization. This shift in plan design impacts how pharmacy benefits and medical costs are managed, directly affecting risk-sharing and cost containment strategies for plan sponsors.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Mon, 09 Nov 2026 20:00:38 GMT

articles.title: FDA Mandates Vision Loss Warnings for GLP-1 Medications
articles.summary: The FDA has instructed GLP-1 manufacturers to include warnings regarding a potential vision loss side effect on their product labeling. This new safety requirement could influence clinical decision-making, prior authorization criteria, and employer risk assessments as self-funded plans evaluate ongoing coverage for these high-cost drugs.
articles.source_line: Source: The Washington Post; Tue, 10 Nov 2026 03:19:56 GMT

articles.title: Trump Administration Targets 340B Drug Discount Program for Major Reform
articles.summary: The Trump administration is moving forward with reforms to the 340B drug discount program, drawing pushback from hospitals concerned about financial burdens. Because 340B policy shifts impact drug pricing dynamics and manufacturer restrictions, any overhaul directly affects self-funded employer health plans and PBM cost containment strategies.

articles.title: New Transparency Rules Increase Scrutiny on Healthcare Insurance Networks
articles.summary: Recent transparency regulations are placing heightened regulatory and market focus on major healthcare insurance networks. This increased oversight directly impacts self-funded employers seeking greater clarity into network pricing, steerage, and total cost of care. Consequently, plan sponsors face growing pressure to demand deeper accountability from their administrators and PBM partners.

articles.title: CVS Health Announces Corporate Split of PBM and Retail Operations
articles.summary: CVS Health is reportedly splitting its business into two distinct entities, separating its Aetna insurance and Caremark PBM divisions from its retail pharmacy network. This massive corporate restructuring could dramatically alter the competitive landscape for self-funded employers contracting for pharmacy and medical benefits. Plan sponsors will need to monitor how this structural shift impacts PBM pricing transparency, integrated benefit delivery, and market competition.
articles.source_line: Source: Law Commentary; Tue, 10 Nov 2026 00:04:37 GMT

articles.title: Representative Matsui Introduces 340B Reform Bill H.R. 10937
articles.summary: Rep. Doris O. Matsui has introduced H.R. 10937, the PROTECT 340B Act, aiming to address rules and operations within the federal 340B drug pricing program. Because 340B program mechanics heavily impact specialty drug costs, manufacturer restrictions, and overall pharmacy supply chain economics, legislative changes are closely monitored by PBMs and self-funded employers.
articles.source_line: Source: Quiver Quantitative; Tue, 10 Nov 2026 01:05:00 GMT
